java_provenance_checked.finding: Display.getCreole reads spriteContainer.getPadding() and passes it to SheetBlock1.
SkinParam.getPadding resolves the global legacy Padding value consumed by Display.
SheetBlock1 stores same-valued padding, expands preferred dimensions by the paired padding amount, and translates atoms by left/top padding before painting.
AbstractTextualComponent builds the note text block through Display and composes that padded sheet with the Rose component margins.
Relationship-owned link notes are Rose note components whose preferred size and drawing both flow through the Display-created text block.

rust_provenance_checked.finding: ResolvedNoteStyle carries sheet_padding from the last parseable global skinparam Padding value for both standalone and relationship-owned Class notes.
note_box_dims and relationship_note_box_dims add twice sheet_padding around the measured body before Rose note margins.
emit_note_body translates body painting by sheet_padding and reduces the available width by twice sheet_padding.

perturbations.key_observation: Java note path spans approximately 231x79 while Rust spans approximately 221x64; Java table grid uses stroke-width 0.5 while Rust uses 1.0. Text and grid positions diverge inside the note as well as layout extents.
perturbations.classification: In-scope counterexample to the broad structured-body claim. The zero-padding table controls also fail, so the immediate root is not just missing padding extraction, but the account claimed structured table atoms were covered by the shared sheet wrapper.

perturbations.key_observation: The note polygon and text positions are effectively aligned, but tree branch primitives differ by stroke-width 0.5 versus 1.0 and tiny coordinate rounding.
perturbations.classification: In-scope structured-note evidence, but not decisive for the sheet-padding math by itself because the same tree primitive stroke mismatch appears in zero-padding controls.

perturbations.key_observation: The table note body is narrower/shorter in Rust than Java and grid strokes differ; the same table-family divergence appears in link-note table controls.
perturbations.classification: In-scope counterexample to the broad structured-body claim.
Shows table primitive parity debt exists even without sheet padding.
Shows tree primitive stroke-width parity debt exists even without sheet padding.
Confirms table-body absolute parity is already failing at zero padding.
Confirms tree branch stroke-width mismatch is already present at zero padding.

verdict.reason: The plain and monospace padding path behaves: Padding 0, positive integer, standalone notes, relationship-owned notes, and several LR/TB positions pass. However, the requested mechanism account explicitly claimed structured note bodies would be covered by the same SheetBlock1-style wrapper, and fresh table/tree perturbations produce in-scope structural diffs. The most decisive failures are table notes: both link-owned and standalone table bodies remain narrower/shorter in Rust and have grid stroke/layout differences. Zero-padding controls show the root cause is pre-existing structured-note primitive parity, not merely missing global Padding parsing, but the broad class-note-sheet-padding claim cannot be accepted while those structured-body counterexamples fail.
verdict.required_followup: Either narrow this mechanism and account to the subset actually validated by fresh evidence, or add a separate causal account and implementation for Class note table/tree primitive parity before re-reviewing the structured-body claim. Preserve these counterexamples; they should remain failing evidence until the structured note painter model is fixed.
